title: Notice Kreyòl Sounds
summary: Start reading Kreyòl by noticing dependable spelling patterns, meaningful accent marks, the spelling ou, and the common nasal patterns an, en, and on.

sketchBlocks.title: Kreyòl spelling gives you useful sound clues
sketchBlocks.bodyMarkdown:
Kreyòl is written with a standardized spelling system. For a beginner, the most useful habit is to **look at the Kreyòl spelling itself instead of guessing from English spelling**.

Start with a few anchor words:

- **bonjou** — hello
- **mèsi** — thank you
- **wi** — yes
- **non** — no

You do not need to memorize every sound today. First, notice that the same written pattern is meant to guide you consistently when the pattern appears again.

tryItExercises.hint: Choose the option that correctly applies the pattern.

sketchBlocks.title: Accent marks and ou matter
sketchBlocks.bodyMarkdown:
Two details are especially useful in your first Kreyòl words:

- **è** is a real part of the spelling. In **flè**, keep the accent when you write the word.
- **ou** works together as one common sound pattern. The word **ou** itself shows the two letters staying together.

Do not silently replace **è** with plain **e**, and do not drop one of the letters in **ou**. Apply these same spelling habits to other familiar words in the practice.

sketchBlocks.title: Notice an, en, and on
sketchBlocks.bodyMarkdown:
Kreyòl also uses common nasal vowel spellings such as **an**, **en**, and **on**. For now, learn to recognize the written patterns in familiar words rather than trying to master every pronunciation rule at once.

Examples to notice:

- **manman** — mother
- **pen** — bread
- **non** — no

Later lessons can refine how these patterns behave in different words. For now, just learn to spot these spellings and keep them when you write.

help.hint_2: Read the complete result aloud once before checking it.
